column1: # The navigation shell hosts Worlds; it must not name one. Each row is one
# product SYMBOL a shell file still names, owned by the phase that removes it.
# Rows are per-symbol, not per-file, for two reasons. A file-keyed row lets an
# already-listed file absorb unlimited new references invisibly — and these are
# exactly the files phases B/C are about to churn. And a symbol survives
# `crate::control::DirtyProject` decouples nothing and records the same row, so
# the ratchet cannot be turned backwards by relabelling a path.
# The gate fails on a NEW row and on a STALE one. The production shell now has
# no product references, so this file is intentionally empty below its header.
